Densify monthly climatologies to daily values

Source: R/densify.R
densify_monthly.Rd

Converts 12 monthly values (one climatological year) to daily values for a reference calendar year. The default "pchip_mp" method fits a cyclic piecewise cubic Hermite interpolant (PCHIP, Fritsch-Butland derivatives as in scipy.interpolate.PchipInterpolator) through the monthly values placed at mid-month and then corrects each month so that the mean of its daily values equals the input monthly value (mean-preserving step).

Usage

densify_monthly(
  tmin,
  tmax,
  year = 2023,
  method = "pchip_mp",
  engine = c("auto", "tempify", "native"),
  consistency = c("check", "mean_range")
)

Arguments

tmin, tmax

Numeric vectors of length 12, or matrices with one row per location and 12 columns (January to December), in degrees Celsius.

year

Reference calendar year. Default 2023 (365 days); leap years give 366 days.

method

Interpolation method. "pchip_mp" (default) or "pchip" for both engines; tempify also offers "linear", "akima", "cubic" and "fourier".

engine

"auto", "tempify" or "native".

consistency

"check" or "mean_range".

Value

A list with matrices tmin and tmax (one row per location, one column per day), the vector of dates, and provenance (engine, method, versions and diagnostics). Rows with any missing month are NA.

Engines

  • engine = "tempify" calls the Python package tempify through reticulate. It is the reference implementation and supports all tempify methods.

  • engine = "native" is a pure R implementation of "pchip" and "pchip_mp" that follows the tempify algorithm (cyclic padding with two nodes on each side, mid-month anchors, uniform monthly correction). It needs no Python and is tested against tempify to within 1e-9 degrees C.

  • engine = "auto" uses tempify when it is importable and native otherwise.

Mean preservation and its side effects

The tempify mean-preserving step adds the residual of each month uniformly to its days. Monthly means are therefore reproduced exactly (up to the convergence tolerance), but the daily curve is piecewise shifted and can show small steps at month boundaries. densify_diagnostics() reports the magnitude of those steps.

Physical consistency

Independent interpolation of tmin and tmax can, in principle, produce days with \(T_{min} > T_{max}\). With consistency = "check" such days raise an error. With consistency = "mean_range" the daily mean \((T_{min}+T_{max})/2\) and the diurnal range \(T_{max}-T_{min}\) are densified instead and transformed back. Because the transformation is linear, monthly means of tmin and tmax are still preserved exactly; an error is raised if the densified range becomes negative. Extremes are never swapped or clipped silently.

References

Rymes, M. D., & Myers, D. R. (2001). Mean preserving algorithm for smoothly interpolating averaged data. Solar Energy, 71(4), 225-231.

Fritsch, F. N., & Butland, J. (1984). A method for constructing local monotone piecewise cubic interpolants. SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing, 5(2), 300-304.

See also

tempify_available(), densify_diagnostics().

Examples

tmin <- c(11, 11, 9, 7, 5, 4, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10)
tmax <- c(29, 29, 26, 22, 17, 14, 13, 15, 18, 21, 25, 28)
d <- densify_monthly(tmin, tmax, engine = "native")
dim(d$tmin)
#> [1]   1 365
# Monthly means are preserved
tapply(d$tmin[1, ], format(d$dates, "%m"), mean)
#> 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 10 11 12 
#> 11 11  9  7  5  4  3  4  5  7  9 10
